correctness.summary: Steiner centering and constant width leave exactly the odd Fourier modes n>=3. Weighted Cauchy-Schwarz gives a sharp two-direction evaluation bound; the relevant cosine series has the closed kernel M(d)=(1-cos d)/2+(pi/2-d)sin d. Explicit positive-curvature truncations approach equality for every fixed d. The antipodal case yields the sharp Steiner-disk coefficient 2pi, and restriction to q-fold modes yields the symmetry constants.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Groemer (1988) proves coefficient 4 for some same-width disk. General Hausdorff and Steiner-disk stability papers and later constant-width Fourier work were compared, but no inspected source states the sharp angular support kernel, its canonical 2pi antipodal consequence, or the q-fold hierarchy. Deyan Zhang (2019) remains a specific full-text priority risk because only its abstract was inspected.

value.summary: The result upgrades a one-number stability bound to an exact sharp angular support kernel, identifies the best canonical Hausdorff coefficient as its antipodal endpoint, and gives a symmetry-resolved hierarchy with explicit smooth sharpness families.

limitations: The comparison body is the Steiner disk.
Sharpness is asymptotic near the disk; no noncircular equality case is claimed.
Only cyclic rotational symmetry is quantified.
The full theorem text of Deyan Zhang (2019) was not inspected.
